section: Course Project: build an Agent System on TACC
summary: The course project requires students to build an Agent System on TACC, featuring a user interface, application backend, and model-serving infrastructure. The system architecture includes components for state management, API requests, and an agent workflow that utilizes tools and data sources. Students must integrate at least one relevant capability from tools such as search, databases, or APIs, and implement logging and evaluation mechanisms.

summary: This page outlines the requirements for a course project involving the selection of a specific use case and the development of both frontend and backend components. The system must include a user interface for task submission and monitoring, along with a backend handling agent workflows, model APIs, and data integration. Students are required to evaluate the system using logs and test cases, reporting metrics and analyzing failures. The final deliverables consist of a code repository, a final report, a demo, and a presentation.

summary: The page outlines two recommended exploration directions for course projects: Task Learning & Adaptation and System Efficiency. Task Learning focuses on improving performance for specific tasks or user groups by quantifying improvements over a baseline. System Efficiency aims to reduce latency or resource usage while ensuring that task quality does not degrade.

summary: This page introduces the STORM project, an open-source system that generates articles with citations, and outlines its potential course extensions. It then details major trends shaping the future of work, including the rise of remote work, the integration of automation and AI, and the adoption of hybrid work models. The text also discusses the impact of these shifts on employment skills, highlighting both opportunities for new roles and challenges such as job displacement.

summary: The project is structured into four main milestones: team formation, topic selection, development, and final presentation. Teams of 3-5 students must submit a two-page proposal by October 29 detailing their motivation, system, and evaluation plan. The development phase involves implementing and refining the system based on feedback, culminating in a final presentation with a demo and code repository submission.
